Data DAOs are DAOs whose mission revolves around the preservation, curation, augmentation, and promotion of high-value datasets.
Examples of Data DAOs include large genomic or research databases, historical indexed blockchain chain and transaction data, rollup data, the Wikipedia, NFT collections, and metaverse assets.
Stake in Data DAOs can be tokenized.
The value and utility of data can be objectively expressed and transacted with in markets, in exchange for services to be performed or offered on the data.
Interested parties could harvest tokens in a DAO-driven decentralized compute fabric by analyzing datasets, performing scientific and ML modeling, calculating statistics, and more.
Stakeholders could spend tokens to incentivize the production of raw data, such as sensor data collection, generative art, and human tasks like transcription and translation.
The Filecoin Virtual Machine (FVM) makes it possible to implement all the ingredients to make Data DAOs a reality.
The FVM creates composable layers that can be combined together to form different kinds of DAOs.
Many common-good datasets rely on stewarding organizations to ensure their preservation and continued accessibility.
Examples of common-good datasets include crime statistics, inflation metrics, election results, and environmental data records.
When the responsibility of data preservation lies on a single organization, it can create a central point of failure and trust.
If a single organization goes away or changes motivation, the common-good data could be lost forever or manipulated.
With Filecoin actors, the responsibility of ensuring the liveness of valuable data can be shared collectively.
Permissionless code running autonomously on-chain can guarantee the continuation and renewal of storage.
Content-addressing ensures that the underlying datasets cannot be modified or altered.
Funding mechanisms and decision-making can be coupled with Data DAOs and Staking Protocols to enable pay-once-store-forever mechanics.
